title: New Jersey DUI Lawyer Rachel Kugel Discusses Signs That a DUI Case Is Weak
text:
New Jersey DUI Lawyer Rachel Kugel Discusses Signs That a DUI Case Is Weak By: AB Newswire February 20, 2025 at 17:30 PM EST New Jersey DUI lawyer Rachel Kugel ( https://thekugellawfirm.com/signs-that-a-dui-case-is-weak/ ) explains the key indicators that may weaken a DUI case and how these factors can impact a defense strategy. DUI charges in New Jersey come with severe penalties, but not every case results in a conviction. Understanding the potential weaknesses in a case can help individuals facing charges assess their legal options. At The Kugel Law Firm, Rachel Kugel and her team closely examine every aspect of a DUI case to identify flaws that may be used to challenge the prosecution’s claims.
One of the most significant factors that can weaken a DUI case is how evidence is gathered and handled. New Jersey DUI lawyer Rachel Kugel highlights that law enforcement officers must follow strict protocols when conducting field sobriety tests, administering breathalyzer exams, and handling blood alcohol content (BAC) samples. Any deviation from these procedures can lead to unreliable evidence that may be challenged in court. BAC tests, for example, must be conducted using properly calibrated devices, and officers must observe suspects for at least 20 minutes before administering a breathalyzer test. Failure to adhere to these protocols can result in questionable BAC readings.
Another issue that can impact the strength of a DUI case is the reliability of field sobriety tests. These tests assess a driver’s coordination and cognitive function, but they can be affected by external conditions such as uneven pavement, poor lighting, or a suspect’s medical conditions. New Jersey DUI lawyer Rachel Kugel points out that law enforcement officers rely on their own observations, which can sometimes be subjective. If a suspect was nervous or physically unable to perform the test due to an unrelated condition, the results may not accurately reflect impairment. Additionally, video evidence from dashcams or body cameras can provide an unbiased view of a suspect’s behavior during a traffic stop. If the footage contradicts the officer’s account, it may cast doubt on the prosecution’s case.
For a DUI charge to hold up in court, the arresting officer must have had reasonable suspicion to make the initial traffic stop. If the stop was conducted without a valid legal reason, any evidence collected during the encounter may be inadmissible in court. Rachel Kugel stresses that constitutional rights must be upheld throughout the process, and failure to do so can lead to a case being dismissed. Officer bias can also play a role in DUI cases. Since much of the evidence is based on an officer’s observations, inconsistencies in their testimony or improper administration of sobriety tests can be challenged. If an officer’s conduct is found to be biased or flawed, the prosecution’s case may be significantly weakened.
Another factor that can impact a DUI case is whether law enforcement properly informs the suspect of their rights. Miranda rights must be read during an arrest, and failure to do so can result in certain statements being excluded from court proceedings. Additionally, in cases where a suspect refuses a BAC test, officers are required to explain the legal consequences under New Jersey’s implied consent law. If an officer fails to provide this warning properly, the refusal charge may be challenged.
There are multiple legal defenses that can be used to fight DUI charges, and questioning the legality of the traffic stop is one of the most effective. If an officer did not have a legitimate reason to pull someone over, any evidence obtained during the stop may not be admissible in court. This can include BAC test results, field sobriety test performance, and officer observations. Rachel Kugel emphasizes that challenging the accuracy of sobriety tests is also a crucial defense strategy. If an officer did not follow standardized procedures or administered the tests in poor conditions, the results may not be reliable.
The integrity of BAC testing is another critical issue. The prosecution must prove that the blood sample was properly collected, stored, and analyzed. If there are any gaps in the chain of custody or evidence of contamination, the BAC results can be questioned. Rachel Kugel explains that defense attorneys can request documentation of how the sample was handled and analyzed to determine if any errors occurred. If inconsistencies are found, the evidence may be dismissed, which can significantly weaken the prosecution’s case.
Facing DUI charges can be overwhelming, but identifying the weaknesses in a case can help build a strong defense. Errors in police procedures, unreliable BAC test results, and questionable sobriety test performance are all factors that can be used to challenge a DUI charge. Rachel Kugel and The Kugel Law Firm focus on analyzing every detail of a case to determine whether the evidence is flawed and how it can be used to defend against DUI charges. Seeking legal representation early in the process can make a significant difference in the outcome of a case. Rachel Kugel’s knowledge of New Jersey DUI laws allows her to identify weaknesses in the prosecution’s case and develop an effective defense strategy.
